title: The State of MCP observability: Observable.tools — Alex Volkov and Benjamin Eckel, W&B and Dylibso
talk_summary: W&B and Dylibso describe how MCP tool calls create an observability blind spot in agent systems, and show how to fix it by propagating OpenTelemetry trace context through MCP's meta payload so client and server spans stitch into one distributed trace. They demo a working TypeScript/Python example and argue for vendor-neutral semantic conventions for agent spans.

takeaways.technique: Distributed tracing across agent/tool boundaries via OTel context propagation
takeaways.what_they_do: Extract the current span in the MCP client, shuttle the trace context through the protocol's meta payload, inherit it as the parent span in the server, and send both to one OTLP endpoint so the backend stitches the full trace.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to extract our current span and we're going to uh pass it along to the server... shuttling the data through the protocol's meta payload

takeaways.technique: Standardize on OTLP endpoint + auth headers instead of bespoke SDK integrations
takeaways.what_they_do: Point any language's agent at a single OTLP endpoint with authorization headers and a project selector; no per-SDK bespoke tracing code needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just define W&B weave as the OTLP endpoint standard... add authorization headers and specify which project you want to go into

takeaways.technique: Trace-derived per-call duration and metadata for capacity decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: Spans carry duration and arbitrary metadata per step, letting you see where time and calls are spent across the call graph.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a span represents the duration and some arbitrary metadata for each step

takeaways.technique: Agent-queryable trace store via MCP server
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose traces through an MCP server so a coding agent can query and summarize its own telemetry, detect wrong output, and iterate to a fix.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have an MCP server that lets your agents or or chats etc talk to your traces and see the data and summarize the data

takeaways.what_they_do: Define agreed attribute names so backends can recognize a span as an MCP tool call with an error vs an HTTP request, enabling cross-platform queries and alerts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how does it know that it's an MCP tool call that has an error. Um that's where semantic conventions come in
